scope: Corollary 7.3 (Equal-size partners) of the manuscript “A Counterexample to Kurosh’s Division-Ring Problem” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Kuroshs-Division-Ring-Problem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 201 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9195b0a83fc63370), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are r ∈ S and a positive integer K0 with the following property. Let P, Q1, . . . , QK0 be independent small generic inputs of size r. For generic fixed input arrows Uj : P ← Qj, the loop columns and the images of V ↦−→ m(P, Qj; Uj, V ), V : Qj ← P, 1 ≤ j ≤ K0, span TP after extension to the joint field of the data. The analogous assertion holds with the other arrow fixed. The same r and K0 may be used for both assertions.
